title: Quantization Memory and Attribution of Looping Gains
subtitle: BReD · LoopTitan · Progressive Distillation
intro: Main reads examine EMA-state quantization and controlled parameter-revisit experiments. Briefs cover data allocation, a new Wharton-authored paper and research blogs. The classic derives two-teacher-step to one-student-step diffusion distillation.
window: November 23–26, 2026 (America/New_York; emphasis on updates since the previous issue, with a 72-hour overlap)

articles.paper: BReD: Block Replay Dithering for Stable Low-Bit EMA Optimizer States
articles.authors: Zhan, Heshen · Huang, Youhan · Peng, Yunke · Wang, Yao · Kong, Linghui · Zhu, Ziwei · Han, Qingyu · Wang, Yaoyuan · Chen, Congliang · Sun, Ruoyu
articles.title: BReD: how momentum remembers small bias

blocks.text: Let s be the full-precision EMA driven by the same input sequence, sᵈᑫ the dequantized state and e=sᵈᑫ−s. Each write-back injects ε. The paper first isolates storage error; it does not assume that gradients along two parameter trajectories coincide. [1]

blocks.label: Paper theorem: ξ is temporally independent, zero mean, with second moment σ²; the initial state has finite second moment and is independent. β∈(0,1). Bias is amplified faster as β approaches one.
The paper’s local non-clipped interval model: p₀ and p₀+Δ are adjacent grid points. Subtractive dithering is unbiased, but does not have smaller variance than stochastic rounding at every x.

blocks.text: BReD replays the same random value keyed by state, step and block. Sharing dither within a block reduces generation cost and introduces correlation. It compresses persistent states while preserving optimizer computation and hyperparameters. [1]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The table summarizes evaluated settings, not guarantees for every task. Embedding states remain full precision during pretraining. The EMA theorem is not a full Muon convergence proof with clipping, correlated errors and closed-loop gradients. [1]

articles.paper: LoopTitan: What Does Parameter Revisit Buy a Mixture-of-Experts?
articles.authors: Tian, Zichen · Lu, Yudong · Wu, Xuansheng · Zou, Na · Hu, Xia · Wang, Guanchu · Sun, Qianru
articles.title: LoopTitan: make weight sharing the final ablation

blocks.text: The main setting uses 1.3B stored and 0.2B active parameters with 5B DCLM tokens. Network shape, expert layout and residual scale are changed before sharing middle-layer parameters. The non-revisit control spreads experts over more independent layers. [2]

blocks.label: Paper Proposition 1: a is a residual multiplier and W a branch-ending output projection. It requires the same batches and no gradient-norm clipping; Muon must not hit its normalization floor, and AdamW additionally needs ε→ε/a.

blocks.text: Residual scaling therefore changes initialization, effective learning rate and weight decay together, so its benefit cannot be assigned to recurrence alone. The non-shared control retains the looped recipe’s gain at matched budgets, but has six extra attention blocks and 1.1% more parameters; matching is not exact. [2]

An extra visit does help when compute increases at fixed parameters. Under Muon, a deeper standard MoE at equal parameters and compute recovers 90.2% of that gain. This is recovery of a local test-loss gap, not a 90.2% improvement in final capability or a training-cost reduction. [2]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The main metric is final test bits per byte. Some comparisons use three seeds and others one. Calling differences below two standard errors a match does not prove that sharing is useless at every scale. [2]

articles.paper: Scaling Looped MoE Language Models under Matched Budgets: Information Flow and Parameter Allocation
articles.authors: Bai, Shipeng · Qin, Jiayu · Liu, Hong · Wang, Xili · Tan, Jianchao · Li, Jiacheng · Zhang, He · Lu, Yifan · Zhang, Jiaqi · Zhang, Kefeng · Xie, Yuchen · Cai, Xunliang
articles.title: Parameter allocation in looped MoE

blocks.text: At matched parameters/FLOPs, gated recurrence and cross-stage residuals use a one-pass Core of 25%–35% of unrolled depth and reallocate saved parameters to experts. After 1T tokens, 69B MLA and 51B KDA gain 1.16 and 2.29 points averaged over four benchmarks. This tests a design package, unlike LoopTitan’s isolated sharing question. [3]

articles.title: Data allocation with a misranking proxy

blocks.text: Data interventions are bandit arms; sparse paired target audits correct arm-specific mismatch without rank preservation. The abstract’s linear-regret risks and change-point bounds rely on stationary/piecewise settings. CivilComments-WILDS is a BERT-Small→Large proof of concept. [4]

articles.evidence: Read abstract/model setting; identity verified through Penn affiliation

blocks.text: New paper coauthored by Qi Long (Penn): latent true covariates, unequal replicate counts, graph-guided precision structure and regression shrinkage are jointly modeled with MCMC. articles.paper: Amortizing Exact Orthogonality: Drift-Triggered Restoration for Orthogonal Fine-Tuning
articles.authors: Zhao, Lanxin · Li, Xiaoyu · Shi, Dai · Gao, Junbin · Han, Andi
articles.title: Drift-triggered polar restoration

blocks.text: RTOFT uses I+S with skew-symmetric S; its orthogonality defect is exactly ‖S‖². Threshold-triggered restoration occurs before the next forward pass. The τ² guarantee requires per-step detection and restoration order, not once-per-epoch repair. This is orthogonal fine-tuning, not a new global Muon theory. [6]

articles.paper: ProPolar: Progressive Polar Decomposition for Implicit Neural Representations
articles.authors: Kim, Pureum · Ryu, Younggeon · Lee, Dongyoon · Lee, Hae Beom · Jin, Kyong Hwan
articles.title: ProPolar: grow the active spectral subspace

blocks.text: Momentum is updated in a low-rank subspace, followed by polar/five-step NS; rank grows progressively while peak learning rate is maintained through growth. INR fitting, super-resolution and NeRF improve. Matched HPO budgets do not imply equal total training time. [7]

articles.paper: Loop Behind: Rethinking Where Extra Loops Pay Off in Looped Language Models
articles.title: Loop Behind: Rethinking Where Extra Loops Pay Off in Looped Language Models

blocks.text: On Dory-4B, most extra-loop gain comes from deeper KV of preceding tokens rather than more current-token computation before readout. Across 12 benchmarks, deeper KV recovers 6.8 of a 7.2-point gap. Loop-Behind overlaps remaining loops with later tokens. That fraction concerns a local accuracy gap, not overall performance. [11]

classic.title: Two teacher steps to one student step: invert DDIM
classic.paper: Progressive Distillation for Fast Sampling of Diffusion Models
classic.dateNote: ICLR 2022; first posted February 1, 2022; read v2: June 7, 2022
classic.question: At fixed total distillation budget, how should updates be allocated across stages to control final one-step endpoint error rather than only local MSE?

blocks.text: DDIM (2020) makes generation deterministic, but reducing steps directly increases discretization error. Salimans and Ho (ICLR 2022) instead train a student to match the endpoint of two teacher steps, repeatedly halving the step count. [14]

blocks.label: Paper setting and DDIM step: s<t, ε is standard Gaussian and log-SNR decreases with t. The second argument of D is the denoising prediction.

blocks.tex: z_s^{\rm teach}=D_{u\to s}\!\left(D_{t\to u}(z_t;\widehat x_\eta(z_t));\widehat x_\eta(z_u)\right),\quad s<u<t
blocks.label: Let zᵤ be the intermediate teacher state. The frozen teacher supplies a deterministic endpoint for a given zₜ; the target is not simply the original x.
Inverting one DDIM step gives the paper’s target. Two teacher steps span one student step. Each student is initialized from the teacher and becomes the next stage’s teacher.
The paper’s v parameterization avoids dividing by α as α→0, unlike ε prediction. Appropriate loss weighting is still required; parameterization alone does not eliminate distillation error.

blocks.text: The paper reports roughly 3.0 FID on CIFAR-10 with four steps under its model, training and evaluation protocol. Teacher endpoint errors can propagate across stages; one-step approximation does not guarantee preservation of every distributional detail. [14]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Read the paper and algorithm; no reproduction. Selection is supported by 3,057 citations in the queried OpenAlex record (November 26, 2026). [15]
